title: Networking
blurb: How the Internet is layered, routed and shared, the protocols that carry the web, and how large companies build datacenter, WAN and edge networks.

main.title: UC Berkeley CS 168: Introduction to the Internet
main.why: Layers, routing and BGP, TCP and congestion control, DNS and HTTP, then datacenters and SDN, with recordings for every lecture. In English.

main.title: End-to-End Arguments in System Design
main.why: Why reliability and correctness belong at the endpoints, the argument behind a simple network core.

main.title: The Design Philosophy of the DARPA Internet Protocols
main.why: The Internet's goals in priority order, and how that order produced datagrams, TCP/IP layering and weak accounting.

main.title: Development of the Domain Name System
main.why: Why DNS is a hierarchy of delegated zones with caching resolvers, and what surprised its designers once deployed.

main.title: A Detailed Look at RFC 8446 (a.k.a. TLS 1.3)
main.why: The one-round-trip handshake, 0-RTT resumption and its replay risk, and the legacy crypto TLS 1.3 removed.

main.title: Congestion Avoidance and Control
main.why: After the 1986 congestion collapse, slow start, AIMD and RTT estimation made TCP back off when the network fills.
Loss is a poor congestion signal on deep buffers, so BBR paces to measured bandwidth and RTT instead.

main.title: The QUIC Transport Protocol: Design and Internet-Scale Deployment
main.why: Google's pre-IETF QUIC, transport and crypto over UDP in userspace, cutting handshake round trips and head-of-line blocking.

main.title: How Facebook is bringing QUIC to billions
main.why: IETF QUIC on Meta's own stack. App heuristics tuned for TCP misfired, and tail latency still fell 20 percent.

main.title: Engineering Egress with Edge Fabric: Steering Oceans of Content to the World
main.why: BGP picks routes without knowing capacity, so Facebook overrides it from a controller to keep peering links from congesting.
Withdrawn routes that linger in the Internet for minutes, and why withdrawing a more-specific prefix makes it worse.

main.title: More details about the October 4 outage
main.why: A backbone command cut every datacenter link, DNS servers withdrew their BGP routes, and Facebook vanished from the Internet.

main.title: A Scalable, Commodity Data Center Network Architecture
main.why: A fat-tree of cheap identical switches gives full bisection bandwidth without big core routers.

main.title: Jupiter Evolving: Transforming Google's Datacenter Network via Optical Circuit Switches and Software-Defined Networking
main.why: Google dropped the Clos spine for optical circuit switches linking aggregation blocks directly, cutting capex 30 percent.

main.title: Data Center TCP (DCTCP)
main.why: Switches mark ECN early and senders cut in proportion to the marks, keeping queues short for small flows.

main.title: Empowering Azure Storage with RDMA
main.why: RDMA across whole Azure regions, with PFC watchdogs, DCQCN tuned across mismatched NICs, and long-haul links.
RoCE for GPU training with PFC and no DCQCN, and why ECMP spread AI traffic badly until each flow used more queue pairs.
Centralized traffic engineering runs Google's inter-datacenter links near full utilization.

further.title: B4 and After: Managing Hierarchy, Partitioning, and Asymmetry for Availability and Scale in Google's Software-Defined WAN

main.title: Orion: Google's Software-Defined Networking Control Plane
main.why: The control plane now running both Jupiter and B4, built as microservices around a pub-sub database.
PoP placement, and anycast against GeoDNS for steering users, with measurements of how slowly DNS drains traffic.

main.title: Maglev: A Fast and Reliable Software Network Load Balancer
main.why: Google's L4 load balancer on commodity servers, with consistent hashing so connections survive backend changes.
nginx's per-worker connection pools wasted handshakes. A shared pool cut new connections 160-fold for one customer.
